subject: Payment ops budget gate + savings hypotheses (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@paygrid.com>; PayGrid Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Payment ops budget gate + savings hypotheses (post-call recap)

Alyssa / team — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pains you called out:
- High per-transaction ML cost at peak (NLP enrichment step) making product margins tight; current LLM spend is ~ $35k/mo for the enrichment pipeline.
- Latency sensitivity for fraud/decline flow (goal < 250ms p95 for enrichment) — can’t trade away SLA.
- Procurement budget is gated this quarter; finance requires an ROI case and a clear runway to net-zero incremental ops cost after pilot.

What we heard as goals:
- Cut unit inference cost by ~40% without hurting p95 latency.
- Demonstrate a predictable path to production (canary > regional rollout) within 8 weeks of pilot start.
- Procurement approval for a constrained pilot spend (target $15k committed).

Redwood hypotheses / levers that map to PayGrid needs:
1) Model + quantization mix: mid-size open model quantized to int8 for 1.2x latency change, 2–3x cost reduction vs hosted large models.
2) Batching + continuous KV caching for repeated prefixes in enrichment (we estimate 25–40% token savings on your pattern mix).
3) Smart routing: place sensitive/latency-critical traffic on a smaller dedicated pool and bulk enrichment on lower-cost capacity.

Initial pilot proposal (high level):
- 6-week pilot: 2-week integration + 4-week live traffic window (sampled 10–15% of production traffic).
- Pilot sizing: we estimate 80M tokens/mo for the sampled workload; see attached pilot-sizing.xlsx for scenarios.
- Success criteria: >=35% reduction in per-transaction inference cost or absolute token-dollar ROI within 30 days of the live window; p95 latency <= 250ms.

Asks / next steps (owners):
- Alyssa: confirm the target sample cohort and whether procurement will accept a 6-week pilot commitment (Alyssa by Mon 6/4).
- Ben: share a short ops checklist and proposed batching config we’d use in the pilot (Ben by Mon 6/4).
- Marissa: draft the commercial/credit ask for finance and propose a pilot pricing sketch (Marissa by Tue 6/5).

Attachments: pilot-sizing.xlsx (scenario tabs: conservative / base / aggressive), redwood-inference-batching-onepager.pdf.

Thanks — I’ll queue up a short tech walkthru next week once Alyssa confirms sample cohort.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Payment ops budget gate + savings hypotheses (post-call recap)

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The $35k/mo figure includes both enrichment and occasional async batches; for the live window we can isolate the enrichment stream you referenced (that’s the one we want to optimize first).
- Procurement is open to a 6-week pilot but will want a capped not-to-exceed for the live sampling portion. If you can propose a credit structure (e.g., limited waived fees up to $X and then usage pricing), that helps us get the internal signoff.

I’ll confirm the sample cohort by Monday. One ask: can you confirm whether the caching approach requires any schema changes on our side (we’re trying to avoid touching the enrichment payload).

— Alyssa
Alyssa Turner | Sr Product Manager, PayGrid
alyssa@paygrid.com | +1 (617) 333-2211

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@paygrid.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Payment ops budget gate + savings hypotheses (post-call recap)

Alyssa — quick ops / tech note on the caching question. Short answer: no schema changes required for basic prefix/KV caching if you route enrichment text through our inference layer as-is. Details: 
- We support prefix keying on the top N tokens and an optional stable key (transaction_id) for per-transaction cache scoping.
- When repeated prefixes show up in your enrichment stream (common templates + merchant names) we can avoid re-encoding the prefix into KV cache which saves 15–30% of prompt tokens in typical billing models.
- Batching: for the sampled 10–15% traffic we’ll use micro-batching to keep p95 latency under 250ms; continuous batching window set to 20ms in the pilot config.

I’ve attached the pilot-sizing.xlsx with an additional tab (ops-estimates) showing expected token counts and a not-to-exceed estimate for three sampling rates. If you want we can hard-cap spend in the pilot by setting an autoscale ceiling + a post-processing quota to prevent overage.

— Ben

ben@redwood.com

Alyssa — thanks. From commercial/finance side I’ll put together two options for the pilot that Procurement can present: 
1) Credit-led: Redwood provides $12k in onboarding/usage credits (applied during the live window) + standard usage beyond that.
2) Discount-led: 35% discount on inference spend during pilot up to a $15k not-to-exceed.

Requesting one hour with procurement to walk through the cost model and the ops protections (hard caps, alerts). If either option looks reasonable I can route a short SOW + DocuSign to get a pilot commitment.

Next immediate steps: 
- Alyssa: confirm cohort and which option Procurement prefers (reply to this thread).
